title: fix(plugin-detail): record:alert resolves its CTA through resolveDeclaredActionIds (objectui#7382)
body:
Fixes #7382
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`record:alert` looked up its optional CTA (`action.actionName`) with its own `find` over the object's `actions` metadata. This was the third hand-written by-name lookup, beside the `resolveDeclaredActionIds` that `page:header` and `record:quick_actions` already share (objectui#7182). The banner now calls that shared function from `@object-ui/types`, as the card's triage (comment `5548547867`) and the seat decision (comment `5827085437`, option C) scope it.

- `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-alert.tsx`: the `ctaAction` lookup passes `ctaName ? [ctaName] : []` (never a list holding `undefined`, which the shared element rule refuses). It passes the object's `actions` only when that value is an array. The lookup reads **only the action-id arm** of the result. The `needsMeta` short-circuit and the `ctaName` line are byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **Why only the id arm:** the shared function treats an array of objects as inline action definitions (`page:header`'s tolerance during its migration). An object authored at `actionName` would take that path and come back as an "action", which would reach the engine and run on click. The old `find` never matched an object, so without the guard the swap would have widened what an alert can run. The guard keeps the slot a name slot.
- **No runtime warning and no new copy.** An unknown `actionName` still renders no CTA and logs nothing, as before. Catching the misspelled name moves to authoring time, in objectstack's `action-name-undefined` lint, filed as https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/20105. That rule today walks neither `record:alert`'s `action.actionName` nor `page:header`'s action ids. The header's own runtime reporter is module-private in `containers.tsx` and its text names the header's surface and key, so reusing it here would have needed a new public export on `@object-ui/components`. The card's first report (comment `5827050915`) has the measurements.
- `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/__tests__/record-alert.declared-action-id-7382.test.tsx`: the pins below. It uses the same data-layer-only doubles as `record-alert.test.tsx`. Here each double RECORDS the metadata name it was asked for and the actions handed to the engine.
- `.changeset/7382-record-alert-cta-shared-resolver.md`: `patch` on `@object-ui/plugin-detail`.

## Pins

| row | holds | measured |
|---|---|---|
| (a) | a known `actionName` renders the CTA, the engine receives the object's registered definition **by reference**, and the first registration wins on a duplicate name (as `Array#find` did); a click executes by name | green |
| (b) | an unknown `actionName` renders the banner without a CTA; the metadata read DID happen, and the engine received nothing | green |
| (c) | no `actionName`, and an empty one, read no metadata (every `useMetadataItem` call carries the `null` no-op name); live control: a real `actionName` does record `sys_user` | green |
| (d) | an object authored at `actionName` (a complete, executable-looking definition) renders no CTA, never reaches the engine, and never executes | green |
| (e) | object metadata whose `actions` is not an array renders the banner without a CTA instead of throwing | green |

## Ablation — on the final head `0f7b3e252`, through `ablation-replace` (anchor hit 1 to 0, blob changed, restored to the HEAD blob `0dd2b01e5f96` with an empty `git diff HEAD`)

- **Leg 1: the hand-written `find` put back** in place of the shared call. **Only (e) goes red** (`TypeError: objectMeta.actions.find is not a function`); (a) to (d) stay green. For every well-formed input the old and new lookups behave identically. That matches the card's "same render" intent, and it is why these rows cannot tell the two lookups apart.
- **Leg 2: the id-arm guard removed** (the result's `kind` checked only against `refused`). **Only (d) goes red**: the object at `actionName` renders a CTA and reaches the engine. This is the row that stops the swap from widening action authority.
- Both runs: `Tests 1 failed | 4 passed (5)`; the lock wrapper `VERDICT command-exit 0`. The same readings were first taken on `97618753a`, before the pin's doubles were typed.

A verbose run names the pin's five rows, the `page:header` id suite, the two #7182 suites and `record-alert.test.tsx`: `Test Files 5 passed (5)`, `Tests 52 passed (52)`.
- Type-check: dependency closure built first (`pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter "@object-ui/plugin-detail^..." build`, exit 0), then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail type-check` echoed `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, exit 0. `--listFiles` on the test project includes the new pin (1 hit).

- Also implicated and green: `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:phantom-deps` (the new value import from `@object-ui/types` is a declared peer), `check:action-ref-convention`, `check:action-forward-parity`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:handler-key-reads`.

So this diff cannot move a verdict on any untouched file. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- **Census for a fourth site** (`git grep -n "\.find((a) => a\.name ===" -- packages/`): 6 hits and no fourth site of this mechanism. Two look up AI agents (`AiChatPage.tsx`, plugin-chatbot `useAgents.ts`), one is a test fixture, two are Studio design-time code (the metadata-admin action picker's label fallback, and `ObjectActionsPanel` selection), and one is this card's site. Outside the regex, `useNavRunAction.ts` matches a URL `runAction` intent against a surface's already-resolved actions, which is a different mechanism.
- `check:changeset-claims` asks for a re-read of two pending changesets that name `record-alert.tsx`: `record-alert-cta-label-i18n-4998.md` and `record-alert-row-binding-4807.md`. Both were re-read, and this diff makes neither false; it touches only the CTA lookup, one import and the docblock. Unrelated drift, noted and not changed here: the #4998 paragraph still calls the renderer's local interface `RecordAlertProps`, a name objectui#7265 already changed to `RecordAlertRendererProps`. Carrier: none.
- The `react-i18next` "pass in an i18next instance" line on stderr is the harness's usual notice; `record-alert.test.tsx` and the #7182 two-renderer suite print the same one.
